content.title: Gary Player's son has lifetime Masters ban for 'tacky' stunt
content.text: Honorary starter Gary Player will once again take part in the ceremonial opening tee shot at the Masters event on Thursday, but he will do so without his son, Wayne. An incident at the 2021 edition of the tournament resulted in his son receiving a lifetime ban from Augusta National. Three-time Masters champion Player, who has won nine major titles in total, has been a fixture of the honorary starters tradition since 2012, teeing off alongside legends such as Arnold Palmer, Jack Nicklaus, and Tom Watson to officially kick off the tournament. • Phil Mickelson behavior toward Masters locker room staff in parking lot after win said it all • Masters champion went on drunk 7 am run after booze-fueled night of partying Yet the moment was overshadowed as Elder stepped onto the tee box, when Wayne, now 61, pulled a shameless marketing stunt. He positioned himself behind Elder – who tragically passed away later that year – during his introduction, brazenly displaying a box of OnCore golf balls, a brand that sponsored Player. Sharp-eyed fans were quick to call out Wayne's actions, and Augusta National wasted no time in responding, stripping him of his tournament credentials and issuing a permanent ban from the course. Augusta National declined to publicly address the incident or the subsequent action taken against Player's son. Wayne opened up about the incident in a 2022 interview with Golf Digest, saying: "Well, they say there's no such thing as bad publicity. I found out that that's not quite true. "I had probably 50 texts after that, 40 of them said I'm a marketing genius, 10 were like, 'What the hell were you thinking?' It wasn't premeditated, but it was a tacky thing. "I don't mind letting people know. To be completely transparent, I think it is a cool story because, you know, the National never really came out formally and said, 'Oh, we're not allowing Wayne Player to come back to the Masters.' • PGA Tour's most outrageously dressed star unveils Masters outfits • Tiger Woods' second mugshot in inmate uniform released as golf legend leaves country "They never ever said that to the media. That's just the way they do it. They don't say much." Despite penning a letter of apology following the incident, Wayne was unable to get the ban reversed. "It said thanks but no thanks," Player recalled of the club's reply. "It said, you know, we appreciate you reaching out and apologizing, we accept your apology, but we are not changing our position, we are not going to allow you back. You ruined a special moment in the history of the game of golf." It comes after Fred Couples laid his feelings on the line with a highly charged Tiger Woods response. Gary Player and his son, Wayne, were caught up in controversy at the 2021 Masters © Augusta National via Getty Images Gary Player of South Africa with his son Wayne Player on the first tee during the final round of the 2022 PNC Championship © David Cannon, Getty Images ; ; ; NASA's supersonic plane could fly London to New York in under 4 hours Kevin Kisner forced to issue apology after blunt criticism of CBS' Masters coverage Taylor Swift’s famous pals organizing wild bachelorette party before Travis Kelce wedding Sponsored Content Angel Cabrera pulled back the curtain on the treatment he received at this year's Masters Club dinner.Last Tuesday, Rory McIlroy, who wanted wife Erica Stoll to 'punch' him, hosted esteemed Green Jacket holders to the Augusta National clubhouse for the Champions Dinner - a tradition unlike any other that dates back to 1952. Though Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson were notably absent from the time-honored gathering, Cabrera made an appearance for the second consecutive year.While speaking to reporters at this week's Senior PGA Championship, Cabrera revealed that he was warmly greeted by McIlroy and company."Yes, I enjoyed this," he said of the Champions Dinner. "I've been with these guys for so many years - 30 years - so we had a great time." Though Cabrera's return to the Masters swiftly drew a fierce wave of backlash given his rocky past, the 2007 U.S. Open champion stressed that he wanted to "do things right in this second opportunity.""I'm very grateful and obviously the people of the golf world are very great with me and I just appreciated the way they treated me," Cabrera said at the time.Addressing the criticism directed his way, he added: "I respect their opinion and everybody has their own opinion and I respect that. Life has given me another opportunity, I got to take advantage of that and I want to do the right things in this second opportunity. Over the last decade-plus, Cabrera has enjoyed a front row seat to McIlroy's rise and fall at Augusta. In 2011, the Argentine was in the same group as the Northern Irishman as he squandered a four-shot lead on the last day of the Masters en route to shooting a final-round 80 and finishing T15.Ahead of McIlroy's inaugural Masters win at the 2025 major, Cabrera wished him good luck in a touching note. "What came out of me on the last green there in the playoff was, you know, at least 11 years, if not 14 years of pent-up emotion," McIlroy said in his post-round press conference."You know, since 2011, I think it's so ironic, as well. I got to my locker this morning and I opened it up, and there was a note in there from Angel Cabrera, and just wishing me luck. And Angel Cabrera was the player I played with on the final day in 2011. It was a nice touch and a little bit ironic at the same time. It's been 14 long years, but thankfully I got the job done."It comes as McIlroy lost $1.7M in prize money just days after his Masters win. Angel Cabrera and Rory McIlroy © Getty ; ; Daniil Medvedev hit with financial punishment over 40-second Monte Carlo outburst Charlie Chaplin's body was once snatched from his grave in shocking ransom demand Syria takes control of all former US military bases on its territory Sponsored Content Golf fans were not happy with coverage of The Masters from ESPN's "First Take." And we don't blame them.Monday morning, after Rory McIlroy won his second straight Masters, finishing the 2026 tournament at -12, Stephen A. Smith and Brian Windhorst discussed the first major of the year. Why is Brian Windhorst covering The Masters for ESPN's biggest morning show? Windhorst is apparently a big golf fan, but it's not something he's known for.ESPN's "First Take" spent much of the time discussing the controversy involving McIlroy's win. Some in the sports world have accused McIlroy of getting too many practice rounds in at Augusta National. Others in the golf world have said that it's no big deal.Smith took the side of McIlroy having an advantage.“I don’t know how anybody else feels about that. He didn’t break any rules, didn’t violate anything. I’m not saying that, please don’t get me wrong. But what I am saying is that does give you an advantage. Not only familiarity with the course because you’ve been playing there for years, but you’ve been there over the last few weeks. That’s what he said. And saying that, you have some people that will believe from a gentleman’s perspective that was an unfair advantage. I don’t think it should take anything away from what we saw him do. I respect the man; he’s a two-time Masters champion right now. We all know he’s one of the greatest golfers in the world, but I did think that was important to bring that up with you,” Smith said.Golf fans, meanwhile, ripped ESPN for the segment"Anyone playing in the Masters can make scouting trips. Non-ball knowers trying to make this a story when it’s literally nothing new and everyone does it," one fan wrote."This is what happens when non-golf fans have an opinion about golf. This is not a new thing. Tiger did this every year and was praised for his hard work and focus, now golf is hitting these non golf watchers and they’re spewing nonsense," one fan added."Great, two people who have no idea what they’re talking about when it comes to Golf," one fan added."Stick to your sports. Most players on the tour can get that amount of practice time. Kevin Kisner and lots of pros say it doesn't make a difference and others like rose or Scott had way more time at ANGC than Rory," one fan added."Really! What utter inane gobbledegook. Do these guys know ANYTHING about tournament play at the highest level. Wasted a few minutes of my life listening to this drivel," one fan added.Golf fans won't be tuning into First Take's coverage moving forward, it appears. ; NFL fans continue to be annoyed with streaming plans for 2026 Female NFL reporter Crissy Froyd fired after trashing Dianna Russini Ryan Lochte's divorce has unfortunately taken an ugly turn Sponsored Content
